findings.title: Embed template has invalid ERB and will not render
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` is not valid ERB/Ruby (it must be `<% end %>`). Rendering `embed/best` raises a syntax error, so every successful embed that already has a topic returns 500 instead of the discussion iframe.

findings.title: raw_html posts skip cooking and sanitization
findings.body: When `cook_method` is `raw_html`, `cook` returns `raw` unchanged and never runs the normal pipeline or Sanitize. Feed and readability imports store that HTML as the post body (`TopicEmbed.import` sets this cook method and `skip_validations: true`). The embed view then emits it with `raw post.cooked`, and the forum will too. A feed item or fetched page can therefore inject script/markup that runs on the Discourse origin for anyone who views the topic or the embed.

findings.title: Imported URL is interpolated into HTML unsafely
findings.body: The imported-from footer builds `#{url}` from the source URL after only checking that it starts with http/https. A URL containing a quote or other markup (for example `http://evil.test/' onclick='alert(1)`) breaks out of the attribute. Combined with the raw_html cook path, that markup is stored and rendered as HTML.

findings.title: Feed poll crashes when an item has no content
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every SimpleRSS item has an HTML `content` string. RSS 2.0 items usually only have `description`, and `content` is nil, so the hourly job raises NoMethodError and imports nothing. `CGI.unescapeHTML` on that body also turns escaped markup (`<script>`) into live tags before it is stored as raw HTML.

findings.title: postMessage targetOrigin is a full referer URL
findings.body: `parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` passes the full referer (scheme, host, path, and query). `postMessage` requires an origin (`scheme://host[:port]`) or `*`. A path-bearing referer throws, so the parent never receives `discourse-resize` and the iframe stays at its default height.

findings.title: Resize messages accepted from any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl
findings.body: The check is `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, not an equality check against the forum origin. Any `e.origin` that appears inside `discourseUrl` is trusted. For example `http://localhost` matches `http://localhost:3000`, and a short prefix such as `https://forum` matches `https://forum.example.com`. A page on that origin can post a `discourse-resize` message and set the iframe height.

findings.title: Embed controller spec expects a retriever the action never calls
findings.body: The example stubs `TopicRetriever.new` and expects `#retrieve` when no embed exists. `EmbedController#best` only calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)`. That expectation fails, so the new controller spec does not pass and does not actually cover the enqueue path, referer/host mismatch, or the loading template.

findings.title: embed_url is limited to 255 characters
findings.body: `t.string :embed_url` uses the default varchar(255) and a unique index. Article and feed URLs with long paths or query strings exceed that and `TopicEmbed.create!` fails, so those pages never embed and the retrieve job errors instead of importing.

findings.title: Each cache miss synchronously polls the entire feed
findings.body: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline whenever feed polling is enabled and this URL is not yet embedded. That opens the feed with no timeout and imports every item on the request/job that is only trying to fetch one URL. A slow or huge feed blocks the worker, and many distinct embed URLs repeat the full poll.

findings.title: Any embed_url is enqueued after a spoofable referer check
findings.body: Host allowlisting happens only later in `TopicRetriever`, not before `Jobs.enqueue`. The referer check uses a client-supplied header, so a caller can set `Referer` to the configured host and enqueue `retrieve_topic` for arbitrary `embed_url` values. That floods the job queue; URLs that do match `embeddable_host` are then fetched server-side with `open` (no timeout, redirects followed).
